take_homes: The part I hadn't thought about is that nobody outside engineering will write their knowledge down. An org-wide memory depends on that more than on the tooling.
Make the agent cite files, so I can see whether it read my memory or made things up. The competitor-claim test for generic pages is a second quick check.
A style file plus a draft-only scheduled agent is a simple package to hand to non-engineers.

monday.move: Set up the sales-team memory and a draft-only daily risk scan, using the one style file for output.
monday.who: Me, then one sales lead to try it
monday.when: Over the weekend, in front of the sales lead Monday
monday.stop_condition: If the sales lead doesn't read the daily output for a week, I stop.
monday.blocker: Nobody in sales asked for it, nobody owns keeping the memory current, and I haven't checked who will maintain it.

misconception.why: The citation point and the two wrong citations in the phase 5 answer showed me output can look good and still not come from my files. I still think checking is mostly for non-experts, and I skipped the plan review and the summary push-back.

one_line: Fine if you've never built an agent system. I got two or three useful ideas out of it, and the pace is slow for engineers.
